context_requirements: Expression of the drug's direct lipase target (e.g., FASN, MAGL/DAGL, LPL) in the cell line
Active lipid/fatty-acid metabolic flux that can be disrupted
For apoptosis, dependence on lipase-supported survival signaling (e.g., BCL-2 family balance)
Hepatocyte-like or colorectal lineage may increase sensitivity to lipase inhibition
falsifiers: No change in any of the listed proximal or late genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines
Strong proliferation or cell-cycle gene changes at 6 h, which would suggest a faster or different mechanism
No apoptosis or stress-response signature at 24 h despite known lipase target expression
A response pattern identical to generic cytotoxic drugs across all lines, indicating non-specific effects

evidence.supports: Lipase inhibitor orlistat induces apoptosis in B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia cells, supporting a pro-apoptotic effect of lipase inhibition.
MAGL inhibitor JZL184 decreases Bcl-2 and increases Bax, inducing apoptosis in colorectal cancer cells.
Orlistat inhibits HBV infection in hepatocyte-like cells, indicating lipase inhibition can affect hepatocyte biology.
Pancreatic lipase inhibitor reduces ROS and inflammatory factor expression in preadipocytes.

changes: Removed GADD45A from proximal_up: no evidence that lipase inhibition induces GADD45A at 6 h; it is a generic stress gene and appears only in late_up.
Removed GADD45A from late_up duplicate placement is retained once; it remains in late_up only.
Kept GADD45B in late_up but not proximal_up, consistent with delayed stress response.
No direction changes were required for the remaining genes because the listed up/down assignments are consistent with a slow stress/apoptosis and proliferation-arrest response to lipase inhibition.
No line-response changes were made because the weak/moderate pattern is compatible with known lineage and metabolic context, though confidence remains low.
